tips.text: Taeguk refers to the source of everything in the universe
and the universal law in which everything continuously goes through cycles
of creation and destruction.
Pumse Taeguk symbolizes the root principle of universal philosophy
and is constructed by applying the truth inherent in Taeguk's yin and yang principles.
Taeguk Ija stands for Tae of the eight trigrams
and symbolizes the pond which looks soft on the outside
but is strong on the inside.
Taeguk Ija was designed for the student to train moves in succession
based on advancing the basic moves learned in Taeguk Ija.
We will now take a look at the Pumse of Taeguk Ija.
Taeguk Ija consists of one key move, Olgul Jirugi.
We will now take a closer look at the key move of Taeguk Ija, Olgul Jirugi.
Olgul Jirugi is a move where you thrust your fist in a straight line toward the opponent's philtrum.
Be careful not to let the elbow of your thrusting arm move outward.
That was the key move of Taeguk Ija.
We will now connect the moves in succession and take a closer look at each one.
The key moves of Taeguk Ija first part consist of
Orun Are Makki, Wen Jirugi, Orun An Makki, and Wen An Makki.
When moving the center of your body forward during Apsogi Are Makki,
control your breath, lower your body and set forward.
Then thrust your body with Apgubi.
The moment the foot setting forward touches the ground,
complete the Jirugi simultaneously with the move and breath.
When setting your right foot forward during Orun An Makki,
breathe in while moving the center of your body to your left foot.
Remove any unnecessary force from both feet
and seek the body's optimal condition to perform the Orun Apsogi and Wen An Makki afterwards.
Cautions for Taeguk Ija.
First part, taking a closer look.
Your torso and arms must spin simultaneously.
Move the center of your body and breathe in once the move is complete

The key moves of Taeguk Ija second part consist of
Wen Are Makki, Orun Apsogi, and Orun Jirugi.
The connection of Apsogi and Jirugi should be made so the momentum gained
after the Apsogi folds the kicking leg, resulting in a natural connection with Jirugi.

Second part, taking a closer look.
Be careful not to let your leg rise above your head when performing Apsogi.
It is important that the move connects naturally to Jirugi.

The key moves of Taeguk Ija, third part, consist of Orun Anmakki and Wen Anmakki.
From the Orgul Makki, shift your weight on your right foot,
spin 270 degrees, and perform Doradiki.
When connecting Anmakki, Anmakki, and Doradiki,
shift your weight on your left foot and spin.
Your right arm should face the direction of progress.
Spin the pelvis, which is the center axis, then perform Anmakki with the left arm.
Cautions for Taeguk Ija, third part, taking a closer look.
Be careful not to raise your right leg too much when performing Doradiki.

The key moves of Taeguk Ija, fourth part, consist of Wen Aremakki,
Orun Aptagi, and Orun Jirugi.
The three Aptagi and Jirugi moves must all be performed in succession.
Pay close attention to the connection of each move.
Cautions for Taeguk Ija, fourth part, taking a closer look.
The target for Aptagi is in the front, and be careful not to kick above your head.
